summary: The bill amends the National Voter Registration Act to bar states from registering anyone to vote in federal elections without first receiving and verifying documentary proof of U.S. citizenship, and requires every voter to present an eligible photo ID that shows citizenship or is accompanied by proof of citizenship.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends voter registration procedures to require documentary proof of citizenship and photo ID. It contains no provisions altering federal appropriations, creating new spending programs, or modifying existing budgets. Any administrative costs to states or the Election Assistance Commission are incidental and unquantified in the text.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection.
No provisions relate to health insurance, Medicare, Medicaid, or medical regulation.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

The bill mandates use of DHS systems (SAVE) to verify citizenship status of voter registrants, requires removal of non-citizens from rolls, and directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to initiate removal proceedings under INA §239 when non-citizens are found unlawfully registered. These mechanisms directly leverage immigration enforcement tools and processes.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect defense authorizations or military spending.
No provisions address environmental regulation, emissions, or conservation.
No provisions alter eligibility or funding for welfare, SNAP, housing assistance, or similar programs.
No provisions address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement priorities.

The bill adds new federal criminal penalties for election officials who register applicants without documentary proof of citizenship and for executive-branch employees who assist non-citizens in registering or voting. These are narrowly tailored election-integrity offenses rather than broad sentencing or policing reforms.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export rules.
No provisions address deficits, debt ceiling, or fiscal targets.
No provisions address protections or restrictions based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
No provisions address foreign assistance funding or programs.

The entire bill is devoted to amending the National Voter Registration Act to require documentary proof of U.S. citizenship for federal voter registration and to mandate photo ID (with citizenship indication) for voting in federal elections. It also strengthens removal of non-citizens from rolls and creates related enforcement mechanisms. This is a direct and comprehensive set of stricter voter-ID and election-integrity measures.

The bill requires inter-agency data sharing (DHS, SSA, state DMVs) for citizenship verification and authorizes use of existing SAVE and SSNVS systems. These are limited administrative data exchanges for eligibility checks, not new regulatory frameworks governing technology companies or consumer privacy.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or workplace regulations.
No provisions address religious exemptions, anti-discrimination laws, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
